label: Majaheem

links.name: Frontiers in Veterinary Science / Animals article (10.3389/fanim.2023.1270230)

names.text: Only 'Majaheem' is named in the opened article; the other spellings and 'Majaheem camel' come from the item's given names (earlier research, not checked against a page). 'Najdi camels' comes from a WebSearch result's text (from a WebSearch result text), not opened, and the paper it came from is not identified.

about.text: The Majaheem is a large dromedary breed used mainly for milk in the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf countries. Its milk production traits are described as favourable, but the source gives no yield figures for the breed.

sources.text: Opened with WebFetch: 'one of the breeds most used for milk production, particularly in the United Arab Emirates and in other Gulf countries'; 'favorable milk production traits'; 'the Majaheem camel breed, the animals of which are large'. The article is by staff of Bulaida Farms and describes the breed largely from the authors' own observations.

origin.place: Najd and Dawaser Valley, north and north-east Saudi Arabia (believed)

links.name: IJAR BF-2069 (Indian Journal of Animal Research, June 2026), listed in search results

sources.text: Found in the text of a WebSearch result, not opened: 'The Majaheem breed is believed to have originated in Saudi Arabia, particularly in the Najd and Dawaser Valley regions in the north and northeast.' The search did not show which of its listed pages carried that sentence, so the URL given is a candidate, not confirmed. No formation years found.

Found in the text of a WebSearch result, not opened: a ten-month study of second-calving she-camels where Majaheem produced about 2576 kg of milk in total lactation. The result text does not say the study was in Saudi Arabia or which page it came from; 'where' is set to SA on the strength of the study being a Saudi trial as the result describes it. Lactation length not stated, so no lactationDays.

Opened with WebFetch: the breed is 'described as used mainly for milk'; the article says it is 'one of the breeds most used for milk production' and never labels it dairy or dual-purpose explicitly. 'Dairy' is taken from that description.

gaps: Searched for and not found: a DAD-IS entry or population count for the breed (the DAD-IS URL tried returned 404); UAE or herdbook population figures; milk composition; lactation length and annual yield; formation years. The 2576 kg figure and the origin come from search-result text, not from pages opened, and are not confirmed against the original papers. Wikipedia's camel milk page does not name the breed.
